item.title: Minecraft hotel to open near London as gaming-themed travel goes up a level
item.description: A new 69-room Minecraft hotel is coming to the UK, joining a growing crop of properties designed to let fans step inside their favourite games.

item.title: Chinese-run Brussels networking club raises intelligence concerns
item.description: The Global CEOs Dinner Club brings business leaders and political figures together at high-level events in Brussels and is now seeking to expand into France.

item.title: Hungary cuts German activist Maja T.'s jail term over 2023 attacks at far-right rally
item.description: Last year, Maja T. staged a 40-day hunger strike to protest the "unlawful handover" and "inhumane" prison conditions, an allegation denied by Hungary's prison service.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | September 30th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this September 30th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: US ambassador slams EU's 'Buy European' weapons push as ‘self-interest’
item.description: Preference for European-made arms could disrupt the transatlantic defence industrial base and benefit Europe’s "enemies", Ambassador Andrew Puzder warns.

item.title: No, Macron isn't planning to trigger a war with Russia to stay in power
item.description: Allegations are circulating online that Macron will put France at war with Russia to postpone elections and stay in power as his second consecutive term comes to an end. However, the country's constitution makes this unfeasible in many ways.

item.title: Deadly Russian attacks on Ukraine kill at least four and hit Kyiv power supply
item.description: Ensuring energy supply is critical as the cold winter months approach. Russian strikes on the sector last year cut light and heating as temperatures plunged to as low as -20C.

item.title: Mental health under strain: Spain lags Europe in access to psychologists
item.description: With six clinical psychologists per 100,000 people, against nearly 18 in Europe, regular therapy in Spain is out of reach for many; the alternative is costly private care.

item.title: Flooding and destruction as Hurricane Polo hits Mexico
item.description: Hurricane Polo has caused flooding and damage in parts of Mexico, with aerial footage showing inundated streets and ground images showing damaged roofs, fallen branches and residents clearing debris.

item.title: Belgian minister Theo Francken warns Europe: 'Everything has to go faster' on defence
item.description: Belgian Defence Minister Theo Francken told the Euronews Defence Summit in Brussels that Europe faces a “dark winter” of Russian hybrid attacks and urgently needs stronger air defences, describing Russia as the biggest threat to Belgium’s security.

item.title: World's tallest wind turbine reaches final height in Germany's former coal mining region
item.description: Winds are stronger at higher altitudes, allowing for twice as much energy to be produced.

item.title: Flydubai planes makes emergency landing after fight between pilots
item.description: FlyDubai flight FZ1073 to Israel made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia after a fight reportedly broke out between the pilots, injuring one of them, and an emergency alert was activated, triggering a major security response in Israel.

item.title: Unlike the EU, Trump's new AI pact lets tech companies police themselves
item.description: Tech bosses from Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic signed a White House pledge on Tuesday to keep their AI in check, with no legal force behind it. In the EU, the same companies face fines of up to 3% of global turnover if they break the rules.

item.title: Rehabilitated green sea turtle Jurassic returns to Atlantic
item.description: Jurassic, a 215-pound adult male green sea turtle, has been released back into the Atlantic Ocean after rehabilitation in Florida, equipped with a satellite tracker to monitor his movements.

item.title: Russia is ‘testing how far it can go' before the EU reacts, says Tsikhanouskaya
item.description: Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya believes change in Russia could begin with change in Belarus, arguing that her country’s opposition movement is “more consolidated” than its Russian counterpart.

item.title: Gene therapy: The breakthrough that inspired Spider-Man | Euronews Tech Talks
item.description: Although an inspiration for science fiction movies, gene therapy is real. Here is how it works and what could be improved about it.

item.title: The birth of a painting: Artist Merike Estna on creating in public at the Venice Biennale
item.description: Estonia artist Merike Estna did something extremely unusual for the Venice Biennale, even by its own standards. Over the past five months, she created paintings live in front of daily visitors. The result is 22 canvases which explore the themes of motherhood and feminism.

item.title: Exclusive: Germany shields parts of Deutsche Börse from EU oversight
item.description: The EU is negotiating a reform in Brussels to better integrate its capital markets. Germany has secured an exemption for major European operator Deutsche Börse’s domestically focused trading venues from centralised supervision, leaving a key part of the system under regional control.

item.title: Europe's security and defence in focus amid escalating hybrid threats
item.description: Good morning. This is Mared Gwyn in Brussels, where Euronews’ Defence and Space Summit is just about to get underway – more on that below. Also in this edition: an exclusive interview with the head of President Zelenskyy’s office, Kyrylo Budanov.

item.title: Underground fire: Blaze in German lignite mine cannot be extinguished
item.description: Sparked by a forest fire, hardly any flames are visible above ground, yet underground it still smoulders on a former lignite site in Thuringia and could burn for years.

item.title: Euronews Defence Summit: US ambassador warns 'Made in Europe' alienates NATO allies
item.description: NATO Secretary General, EU and top US officials join Euronews' Defence and Space Summit in Brussels on Wednesday as Europe seeks to strengthen its defence capabilities, respond to hybrid threats and develop a more integrated industrial base.

item.title: Fuel prices above €2 per litre: Who will foot the biggest bill in Portugal?
item.description: From fishing to agriculture, and from freight to passenger transport, many sectors have felt the impact of sharp fuel price rises in Portugal since the start of the Iran war.

item.title: Europe Today: NATO chief Mark Rutte joins Euronews' Defence and Space Summit in Brussels
item.description: Euronews hosts its biggest-ever news event, the Defence & Space Summit in Brussels, with NATO chief Mark Rutte among the guests. Meanwhile, Ukraine races to build interceptor drones against Russia's jet-powered strikes, and Estonia blames Russia for an arson attack on a defence firm.

item.title: Seoul suspects Zelenskyy revealed North Korean POW transfer to win arms support
item.description: South Korea has so far not provided lethal weapons to Ukraine, citing a domestic ban on militarily aiding countries at war.

item.title: What does it mean to be an 'associate member' of the EU?
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen proposed an ‘Alliance for the Future’ that could make Canada the EU's first ‘associate member’. But what is an ‘associate member ’, and what does this alliance mean for the EU and Canada? Watch the video!

item.title: North Korea slams South's claim it was behind DMZ mine blasts, calling it a 'farce'
item.description: North Korea in recent years has added mines, anti-tank barriers and other front-line fortifications, raising concerns in the South about the growing presence of North Korean soldiers near the border.

item.title: Luxury compound uncovered inside Indonesian prison
item.description: Five prison officials have been suspended after an inspection uncovered an apartment-style compound with luxury amenities allegedly being used by inmates at a prison near Jakarta.

item.title: ‘Europe is ending its addiction to a toxic, costly drug’: Heat pump sales soar as electricity taxes fall
item.description: Heat pump sales plummeted in 2024 – but now they’re on the rise again. Here’s why.

item.title: Majorca vs Menorca vs Ibiza: Which of Spain’s Balearic Islands should you visit?
item.description: They may be part of the same archipelago, but Majorca, Menorca and Ibiza each have their own distinct character. Here’s what to know before booking.

item.title: Albanian PM says fate of Kushner-linked luxury project will be decided by 'science', not 'ideology'
item.description: Albania has previously promised that the €1.4bn project linked to Donald Trump's son-in-law will meet EU environmental standards.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | September 30th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this September 30th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Diesel taxes in Europe: Which countries charge the most?
item.description: Diesel has overtaken petrol as Europe's most expensive fuel, at a record €2.226 per litre. Yet EU governments still tax it about 12 cents less than petrol.

item.title: Air pollution is slowing down marathon runners, study finds
item.description: Higher levels of nitrogen dioxide on race day are linked to slower marathon times, particularly among non-elite runners, new research suggests.

item.title: Morocco's King Mohammed VI appoints Fatima Mansouri as the country's first female prime minister
item.description: Mansouri is only the second woman in the Arab world to hold the office of prime minister. Her established political career has seen her serve as mayor of Marrakesh and member of parliament previously.

item.title: Top AI and tech firms sign 'morally binding' accord to 'self-police' development after meeting at White House
item.description: The accord comes amid massive global pressure from civilians and lawmakers alike to regulate the industry as reports of the technology breaking out of its confines continue to pile. Last week OpenAI revealed that its agent had hacked into an Australian government website during its testing phase.

item.title: A little known greenhouse gas is quietly harming half of Europeans. This Italian city is hit hardest
item.description: People who suffer from asthma are the most at risk.

item.title: Man City found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of financial rules, Premier League says
item.description: A statement from the English Premier League said an independent commission found that the club had arranged "sham" contracts and agreements to artificially inflate its revenues and reduce its costs.

item.title: Stellantis to halt four French plants for several days over supply shortage
item.description: The Italian-French-American carmaker has been hit by surging demand for electric vehicles, particularly from business customers.

item.title: Ukraine pushes for 'bold action' on Russian assets to plug $78 billion gap in 2027
item.description: Russia's relentless airstrikes are deepening Ukraine's financial gap. As costs rise and the deficit swells, the country is pleading with European allies to tap into the immobilised Russian assets.

item.title: No energy shortages, but a painful winter looms for Europe, top EU energy leader warns
item.description: Europe needs to protect consumers from another energy price shock while making fossil fuels less central to the economy. Emergency measures can soften the immediate blow, but Brussels is warning governments not to let short-term subsidies or tax decisions undermine the green transition.

item.title: Pressure grows within EPP to expel Vučić’s SNS party over Mladić funeral
item.description: The EU’s largest political family linked the participation of senior Serbian officials at Mladić’s funeral to its ongoing scrutiny of the Serbian Progressive Party, which could ultimately lead to its suspension or expulsion from the EPP.

item.title: With two Orbán-era ministers detained, Magyar's 'Operation Purge' takes shape
item.description: Prime Minister Péter Magyar’s “Operation Purge” has entered a new phase with the detention of two former ministers. Holding officials from the Orbán era to account was a central campaign pledge, and Magyar says the drive will now accelerate. Fidesz has denounced the effort as political revenge.

item.title: Spanish company Sateliot to launch five satellites with SpaceX to boost global 5G
item.description: Sateliot is launching five satellites with SpaceX on Thursday, taking its constellation to 11. The Draconis mission will double daily passes, halve revisit time and bolster its 5G NTN IoT connectivity service.

item.title: Euronews Travel & Tourism Summit 2026: Five of the key takeaways
item.description: Figures from across the travel industry joined Euronews in Brussels on 29 September. Here’s the most important things to know.

item.title: French students blockade schools nationwide to demand more resources
item.description: Hundreds of secondary school students blocked school entrances in Rennes and Paris during a national day of action, calling for more staff and funding for education.

item.title: Russian nuclear-capable Tu-95 crashes in Far East, killing six crew members
item.description: The bomber went down near Krasnoyarovo shortly after taking off from the Ukrainka air base, which Russia had used to shelter surviving strategic bombers after Ukraine's Operation Spiderweb destroyed or damaged more than 40 aircraft at Russian airfields in June 2025.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this September 29th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Baku Security Forum puts cross-border threats in focus
item.description: The Baku Security Forum brought together security and intelligence officials from different countries to discuss counterterrorism, emerging threats and stronger international cooperation.

item.title: UK PM Burnham to lay out 'options' for EU relations later this year
item.description: The country's divisive 2016 vote to leave the EU has once again been thrust under the spotlight this year amid mounting calls from leading Labour figures for Britain to re-enter the bloc.

item.title: Nvidia rival AMD bets $8.2bn on the 'godmother of AI' and her virtual worlds
item.description: World Labs builds world models, AI systems designed to understand how objects and spaces behave, allowing them to simulate what might happen when something moves or an action is taken.
